endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Establish and empower interdisciplinary teams that reflect a wide range of capabilities, competencies, demographic groups, domain expertise, educational backgrounds, lived experiences, professions, and skills across the enterprise to inform and conduct risk measurement and management functions.

commentary.bottom_line: No supplied study tests whether maintaining, filing, and following a written safety policy reduces unsafe mental health chatbot responses, and no supplied study documents the hazard itself. The recommendation currently rests on a Utah statutory requirement and a NIST framework statement.

perspectives.view: The evidence base for this recommendation contains zero studies testing the practice and zero studies documenting the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty is therefore rated as no direct evidence. The two endorsements are a statute and a voluntary framework, and neither reports outcome data on chatbot safety.

The supplied excerpt of Utah HB 452 (2025) uses mandatory language and requires a policy that details actions taken to prevent or mitigate adverse outcomes or harmful interactions. The excerpt does not describe affirmative-defense, filing, or compliance provisions. NIST AI 600-1 uses advisory language and calls for interdisciplinary risk teams. Neither source reports outcome data.

commentary.research_gap: No study compares mental health chatbots operating under a filed, followed safety policy with chatbots operating without one on measures such as harmful response rates, crisis escalation to humans, or user adverse events. Researchers also have not assessed whether regulator filing and compliance review detect policy deviations in practice.
commentary.underserved_note: No supplied study tested the practice in any population, so no test included Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy users. The effect of a written safety policy on the users who may rely most on low-cost chatbot mental health support therefore remains unknown.
